build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player fires a grappling hook at anchor points, connects only when an anchor is in range, stays tethered while input is held, and detaches on demand. A visible tether (rope, beam, or line) appears while attached. Score 0 if there is no grapple action, if the hook attaches to arbitrary empty space with no anchor logic, if no tether is ever drawn, or if the player cannot release.

While tethered, the player swings under physics -- pendulum-like motion driven by gravity and momentum, gaining speed through the arc -- and releasing the hook preserves that velocity into a free launch. Chaining a fresh grapple after release without touching the ground should be possible. Score 0 if swinging is a fixed animation with no momentum, if release does not carry velocity, if the player snaps directly to the anchor, or if motion ignores physics entirely.

The player commands more than one kind of grapple -- for example a swing line that builds pendulum momentum and a pull/retract line that yanks the player toward the anchor -- and can switch between them with a readable mode indicator. Each mode creates a different traversal choice. Score 0 if there is only one grapple behavior, if different modes move the player the same way, or if the only difference is a HUD label.

Movement is physical and player-driven: gravity pulls the player, horizontal acceleration/deceleration is readable, platforms support and block, and the player can influence motion in the air or on the swing through steering, pumping, reeling, or air-dashing. Score 0 if there is no gravity, if the player cannot meaningfully influence movement, if platform collisions are absent, or if movement is only menu/grid selection.

Hazards and collision matter: pits, spikes, blades, beams, crushers, or similar hazards kill, damage, or reset the player on contact, and solid surfaces reliably block. A hazard hit produces clear feedback and returns the player to a checkpoint or failure state. Score 0 if the player passes through hazards harmlessly, if there are no hazards/pits, or if collision is absent.

The full loop is connected without restarting the executable: title -> play a course -> result (completion or failure) -> retry or advance. A timer or score measures performance, and reaching the goal completes the level. Every transition is reachable through in-game UI. Score 0 if any transition is missing or broken, if there is no goal/finish, or if retrying requires relaunching.

The game spans at least three visually distinct worlds or biomes, each with its own backdrop, tileset, and identity -- not the same level recolored. At least two visually different worlds are seen during play. Score 0 if there is only one world or if all worlds share an identical look.

Anchor/grapple-target variety: at least three distinct kinds of grapple points exist with different behavior (fixed, moving/drifting, single-use breakable, spring, slide rails, etc.). The kinds are visually distinguishable before the player commits, and their behavior changes the route or timing. Score 0 if there is only one anchor type or if all anchors behave identically.

Hazard and obstacle variety: at least three distinct hazard/obstacle types (spikes, spinning blades, crushers, beams/lasers, moving platforms, etc.) that threaten the player in different ways, and the mix differs across worlds. Score 0 if there is only one hazard type or if hazards are cosmetic.

Each world applies a distinct environmental modifier that changes how movement and swinging play -- for example gusts that push mid-swing, conveyors that drag along the ground, or low gravity that stretches arcs. At least one such modifier is observable altering motion. Score 0 if all worlds play under identical physics.

Movement-tech depth gives a real skill ceiling: at least two distinct techniques such as pumping the swing to build speed, reeling the line in/out, an air-dash/boost, wall recovery, or chaining swings without touching ground, each changing speed, height, reach, or route choice. Score 0 if the only action is fire-and-hold with no way to shape momentum.

Core run state is readable at a glance through a HUD: the timer or score, current world/level, active hook mode, and progress toward the goal are placed in clear non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the timer/score or hook mode is missing or hidden.

The scene is legible during fast movement: the player, rope/tether, anchor points, hazards, platforms, and goal are mutually distinguishable in color/silhouette, and the camera keeps both the player and upcoming traversal choices readable. Score 0 if the player or tether is hard to pick out, if anchors/hazards are indistinguishable from the background, or if the camera loses the player.

Actions and events produce clear visible feedback: firing and connecting the hook, the swing arc, the release/launch, hitting a hazard, reaching a checkpoint, and finishing the goal each show a visible state change (tether appears, motion curves, flashes, particles, panel swap). Score 0 if grapple, swing, release, death, or goal happen with no visible feedback.
A styled title screen is present with the game name, a way to start, and art that establishes the acrobatic/momentum tone. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.

Overall art coherence: the player, anchors, tether, platforms, hazards, world backdrops, and UI belong to a consistent visual language, and each world reads as a coherent themed environment rather than mismatched parts or default plain grey. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles, relies on unthemed placeholder rectangles, or looks like a blank default scene. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Character and object sprite quality: the player avatar, anchor points, and hazards are real sprite art (illustrated, pixel-art, or hand-drawn), not solid-color rectangles or default HTML 引擎 primitives, and the player and different anchor/hazard kinds are visually distinct. Score 0 if the avatar or in-level objects are plain ColorRect/default shapes or indistinguishable colored blobs.

Environment and level art: platforms, terrain, and per-world backdrops use real textured or illustrated art with surface detail, and the worlds are clearly different illustrated settings. Score 0 if levels are uniform color backgrounds, if platforms are plain untextured rectangles, or if worlds are visually identical fills.

Animation and atmosphere: the swing and rope motion, the player's launch arc, hazard motion, hit/death and goal transitions use animation, tween, particles, shake, or trails rather than instant snaps, and the worlds carry ambient life (swaying foliage, drifting clutter, parallax, glowing tech). HUD and UI chrome use styled themed widgets, not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all motion snaps with no easing/effects, or if nothing on screen ever animates during play.
